answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each agent to stake reputation earned through verified work, not just a fresh key: like ships queuing at a wharf, every newcomer must first complete small, auditable tasks under peer review before gaining full trading rights. Reputation then grows slowly toward its zenith only through consistent, useful service, and decays if the agent goes idle or misbehaves, so spinning up a meadow of fake identities buys nothing: each clone starts at zero and must earn its standing one verified job at a time.
